span.p: Enterprise Architects evolve and govern aspects across and between segments to achieve goals and objectives.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 120px; text-align: center; width: 120px;

span.p: Segment Architects evolve and govern capabilities within segments to achieve goals and objectives.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 120px; text-align: center; width: 120px;

span.p: Capability (specialist) designers and builders create and change capability in building blocks to satisfy requirements.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 120px; text-align: center; width: 120px;

span.p: Solution Architects organize capabilities into new or changed solutions delivering services to meet requirements.

span.p: The TOGAF Standard identifies one overall business domain that may be broken down further e.g. business function/process portfolios depending on what a business actually does; e.g., Finance, Manufacturing, Legal, HR, Customer Management, Service, and Support.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 120px; text-align: center; width: 120px;

span.p: The TOGAF Standard identifies three starting information system domains which may be broken down further e.g., (Technology) into Software, Servers, User Devices, Execution Environments, Networks, Buildings, and Mechanical Devices.
